NEVADA
Under authority of the Act of Congress approved June 4, 1897
(30 Stat., 11I, 34-36), and on the recommendation of the Secretary of
Agriculture, it is hereby ordered that the boundaries of the Toiyabe
National Forest as modified by the Proclamation of December io, 1910,
be further modified by eliminating therefrom the following described
lands, in the State of Nevada:
In T. 9 N., R. 33 E., Secs. r, 2, 3, Y0 to 15, inclusive;
In T. 1o N., R. 33 E., Secs. 8, 9, 10, 11, 14, 15, 16, 17, 20 to 27,
inclusive, 34, 35 and 36;
In T. 9 N., R. 34 E., Secs. 1 to 18, inclusive, 21, 22, 23 and 24;
In T. io N., R. 34 E., Secs. 19, 20, 29 to 36, inclusive;
Mount Diablo Meridian.
It appearing proper and necessary, in the interest of equal opportunity
and good administration, that all of such excluded lands subject to dispo-
sition should be restored to settlement in advance of entry, it is hereby
ordered, pursuant to the authority reposed in me by the Act of September
30, 1913 (38 Stat., 13), that such lands, subject to valid rights, shall be
open to actual settlers only under the provisions of the homestead laws for
a period of twenty-eight days from and including 9 o'clock a. in., standard
time, on the fifty-sixth day from and after the date of this order, and there-
after to entry and disposition under any and all of the public land laws
applicable thereto.

vided and perform a

The Executive order of February 14, 1912, permitting employees in
the executive civil service permanently residing in certain incorporated
municipalities adjacent to the District of Columbia to become candidates
for or hold municipal office therein, is hereby amended so as to include the
incorporated municipality of Somerset, Maryland, among those named in
the order. The first paragraph of the order of February 14, 1912, as
amended, will read as follows:
Employees of the executive civil service permanently residing in the
following incorporated municipalities adjacent to the District of Columbia
will not be prohibited from becoming candidates for or holding municipal
office in such corporations:
In Maryland-Takoma Park, Kensington, Garrett Park, Chevy Chase,
Glen Echo, Hyattsville, Mount Rainier, Somerset.
In Virginia-Falls Church, Vienna, Herndon.
This order is recommended by the Civil Service Commission, for the
reason that she same conditions exist in Somerset, Maryland, as in the
other municipalities named in the original order.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
May 5, 1914.

"An act to increase the efficiency of the permanent military establishment
of the United States," approved February 2, 1901, which authorizes the
President to "prescribe the kinds and quantities of the component articles
of the Army ration, and to Iiect the issue of substitutive equivalent articles
in place of any such components whenever, in his opinion, economy and
a due regard to the health and comfort of the troops may so require," the
Executive Order of January 11, 191 1, as amended by Executive Orders of
January 21, 1913 and July 15, 1913, prescribing the Army ration is revoked,
and the following is promulgated for the information and guidance of all
concerned to take effect June 1, 1914.
The kinds and quantities of the component articles of the Army ration
and the substitutive equivalent articles which may be issued in place of

All articles of the garrison and travel ration due a company, or other

the articles; and the quartermaster will pay as savings to the organization

Paragraphs 663 to 671, 686, 687, and 692 of the Consular Regulations
of 1896 are hereby amended to read as follows:
PARAGRAPH 663.
Conso/ida/ing jinvoices. Merchandise purchased or agreed to be
purchased for export to the United States, must not be included in
the same invoice with merchandise obtained otherwise than by pur-
chase or agreement of purchase.
An invoice shall include only one shipment of merchandise from
the same consignor to the same consignee. Merchandise shipped to
different consignees must not be included in the same invoice, but
merchandise purchased or agreed to be purchased in the United States
and shipped to a branch house or agent of the shipper for distribution
or delivery to twvo or more ultimate consignees, may be included in a
single invoice.
Merchandise purchased or manufactured in different consular dis-
tricts in the same country and assembled for shipment to one con-
signee in the same vessel may be included in one consular invoice at
the point of shipment.
In such cases the certified invoice should have attached thereto
the original bills or invoices, if there be any, or extracts therefrom,
showing the price paid or to be paid for each purchase or consignment.
(Paragraph W, Section 3, Act of October 3, 1913).

ment of purchase differs materially from the shipper's declaration on

of this section, be considered the date of exportation. (Tariff of
